comments.content:
The new numbered hydration marker (`<!--[N-->`) is only understood by `if_block` on the client. The generic hydration helpers still only treat the exact strings `HYDRATION_START` (`[`) and `HYDRATION_START_ELSE` (`[!`) as block starts when tracking nesting depth — see `remove_nodes()` in `internal/client/dom/hydration.js` and `assign_locations()` in `internal/client/dev/elements.js`.

Consequence: if an outer block mismatches while a rendered branch contains a nested `{:else if}` chain (e.g. `{#if a}A{:else if b}{#if c}C{:else if d}D{/if}{/if}` hydrated with `a === true` but SSR rendered `b`/`d`), `remove_nodes()` starts at the inner `<!--[N-->`, does not increment depth for it, and stops at the inner `<!--]-->` instead of the outer block close. That leaves stale nodes and an `hydrate_node` that is not positioned at the outer block's end, so subsequent hydration can desync (and dev source locations are mis-assigned). The depth checks need to also recognise numbered start markers (e.g. `data[0] === HYDRATION_START`), or a marker format already understood by those helpers should be used.

comments.content: This `{:else if}` predicate is now duplicated in three places (here, `client/visitors/Fragment.js` and `server/visitors/IfBlock.js`, plus it already exists in `compiler/legacy.js`). More importantly, the two client call sites don't test the same thing: this one inspects the raw `node.alternate.nodes`, while `Fragment.js` inspects the cleaned `trimmed` array. The generated arrow only declares `$$elseif` when *this* check passes, but `Fragment.js` is what decides to reuse the parent anchor instead of creating a wrapper template node. If the two ever disagree (e.g. a non-`IfBlock` node or whitespace node in the alternate fragment), the emitted `$.if(..., $$elseif)` would reference a parameter that was never declared, producing a runtime `ReferenceError`. Suggest extracting a single shared helper (e.g. `is_elseif_block(fragment)` in `phases/3-transform/utils/ast.js`) and using it in both visitors so they cannot drift.

This numbered-marker hydration protocol (server emits `<!--[N-->`, client parses it back into `hydrate_index` and compares it against `root_index`) is brand-new behaviour, but there is currently no hydration or SSR test anywhere that uses an `{:else if}` chain (`grep '{:else if' packages/svelte/tests/hydration` and `.../server-side-rendering` both return nothing). Since correctness depends on the server `index` starting at 1 and matching the client's `root_index` numbering, please add hydration tests covering each branch (first branch, each `{:else if}` branch, final `{:else}`) plus a mismatch case, so regressions in the numbering are caught.

The previous `elseif` parameter documented what this flag meant; the new tuple has no explanation for its two positions or for the sentinel values used by the implementation (`Infinity` for `{:else}`, `-1` to stop checking hydration, and `hydrate_index > root_index` as the "a later branch was rendered" test). This bookkeeping is not self-explanatory, so a short comment (on the param or above the mismatch block) describing what `root_index` (branch position in the `{:else if}` chain) and `hydrate_index` (index of the branch the server actually rendered) mean would make the hydration logic maintainable.
